text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crown Prince Hassan tells emergency meeting of UNRWA donors that solving Palestinian refugee problem is the cornerstone of a just peace in the Middle East.
- Prime Minister Kabariti calls on the opposition to seek solutions instead of personalising their opposition. Tells journalists Jordan seeks best relations with brotherly Arab countries.
- Opposition deputies call on Arab parliaments and leaders to challenge the conspiracies for the Judaisation, division or change to Jerusalem's features.
- Kabariti says national interests are the fundamentals of Jordanian policy. "We want Jordan to be a place of work for the sake of the nation, not a free-for-all".

- October opening of next parliamentary session may be delayed two months, sources say, because of resignation of some deputies and to give time to improve relations between parliament and the government.
- Crown Prince Hassan warns of dangers of ignoring millions of Palestinian refugees.
- Minister of Supply Sobar says Israel agrees to import Jordanian vegetables and fruits.
- New Stock Exchange law will give opportunity to private brokers.
- Jordan prepares for talks next month on joining World Trade Organisation. Officials consider raising sales tax to compensate for customs liberalisation.
- Kuwait's Islamic Affairs Minister due in Amman on Tuesday.
- Kabariti visits General Headquarters of Armed Forces.
